about: Does a request to consolidate a session's work into a plan select plan-conveyor, whose `migrate`
subcommand exists for exactly that? Written 2026-09-29 after two findings: the user reported
consolidation losing depth and ignoring the conversation on three harnesses, and a sweep of every
Claude Code transcript on the author's machine found `migrate start` had never been run on real
work. So the first question is whether the request ever reaches the skill at all.
The positives are phrased the way the request actually arrives: 'write up', 'put everything in a
plan', 'consolidate what we discussed', 'migrate this doc'. None names `migrate`, because a request
that names the command does not test the trigger.
The pair to watch is session-harvest, which owns 'what is worth saving before I stop' and routes
each item to a plan, an AGENTS.md or the home file. The boundary: harvest decides WHERE each
thing goes; plan-conveyor is chosen once the destination is already one plan. Two harvest
positives mark that line from the other side.
The negatives are the look-alikes that want no plan file at all: a summary in the chat, a README
Measured 2026-09-29, run mode against the installed descriptions, 3 runs: 10/10, precision and
recall 1.0 for both skills. So the trigger is NOT why migrate went unused: a cold consolidation
request loads plan-conveyor every time. The gap is after loading, with the migrate section at
line 1,642 of 1,736, which is why the same change added it to the opening 'Start here' table.
What this suite cannot see is a request made late in a long session rather than cold.

cases.prompt: Write up everything we decided in this session, plus the two notes files we made, into one plan.
Consolidate what we discussed today and DESIGN-notes.md into a single plan file without losing the detail.
Migrate this NOTES.md and the reasoning from our conversation into plans/.
Put all the decisions, pitfalls and risks from this conversation into the plan for this feature, and merge in the scratch doc.
We have a draft plan, a research report and this whole discussion. Turn them into one plan and check which of it is still true in the code.
Anything worth saving from this session before I compact?
Harvest this session and tell me if anything is dangling before I stop.
Summarise this conversation for me in a few bullet points.
Add a README section describing the feature we just built.
Write a commit message for the staged changes.
